America must provide objective evidence of proficiency in the English language. However, the
following exceptions apply:

Additional Exceptions for Applicants to Graduate Programs:
1. Applicants who have received a U.S. Bachelor’s or U.S. Master’s degree or who have
completed two years of full-time academic study at an accredited post-secondary institution
within the U.S. or at an Australian, British, Canadian, U.S. or other accredited post-secondary
institution overseas in one of the above countries/territories, where English is the language of
instruction, may be exempted from this requirement after supporting academic records have been
reviewed by the Graduate School at UMBC.
2. Applicants who have successfully completed master’s level coursework at an accredited
postsecondary institution within the U.S. or at an Australian, British, Canadian, U.S. or other
accredited post-secondary institution overseas in one of the above countries/territories, where
English is the language of instruction and that coursework is related to the academic program of
admission, may be exempted from this requirement after supporting academic records have been
reviewed by the Graduate School at UMBC (A grade of B or better is required to be considered).
3. Applicants who have been living and working in the United States for at least 5 years.
Working in a professional setting related to the applicant’s intended program of study is
especially preferred, and a resume/CV should be available for review for assessment of work
history.
4. Applicants who have successfully completed Level 6 coursework within UMBC’s English
Language Institute.
Any request for a waiver of the English language proficiency requirement must be submitted in
writing to the Graduate School at UMBC with any supporting documentation.
UMBC reserves the right to require evidence of English language proficiency for all applicants,
the adequacy of which shall be at the sole discretion of UMBC.
